audit.summary: Archived assessment: Minor. Hajos-coordinate and stable-permutation qualifications; Loop and bridge qualifications in graph decompositions; Simple cut-lattice vectors need not be one directed bipartition cut
limitations: P1 — Hajos-coordinate and stable-permutation qualifications — Counterevidence: The stable move preserves lower triangularity and establishes the intended Lemma2.6; the existence theorem is not refuted.

P1 — Hajos-coordinate and stable-permutation qualifications — Counterevidence: OnceHajos coordinates are chosen the parity proof is correct. Stable movement of the pure-column index tolast preserves the lowertriangular principal submatrix; last-row reduction modulo2 restores entries0/1.

P2 — Loop and bridge qualifications in graph decompositions — Counterevidence: Reduced Tait graphs are loopless and bridgeless; a tiling flow lattice excludes norm1 loops. The intended main link classification is not refuted.

P2 — Loop and bridge qualifications in graph decompositions — Counterevidence: The primaryAAM explicitly makes reduced Tait graphs loopless/bridgeless, and tilingflowlattices cannotcontainnorm1loopvectors. Vertex-sum flow decomposition does not require bothfactors to be2-connected.

P3 — Simple cut-lattice vectors need not be one directed bipartition cut — Counterevidence: For a directed cycle after reversal, pairing with the cut is minus the count of reversed edges and must vanish; hence the same cycle already existed. Unique-short-characteristic proof survives.

P3 — Simple cut-lattice vectors need not be one directed bipartition cut — Counterevidence: The source's broad definition[H]inCut already accommodates the vector. If reversal createsa directedcycleC,cut-floworthogonality gives0=-numberofreversededgesonC, soC wasalreadydirectedbefore.

P4 — Zero stabilization does not characterize reduced diagrams — Counterevidence: Theorem3's normalized determinant condition allows bridge-type curls consistently with the recursive single-edge base; it excludes loop contributions.

P4 — Zero stabilization does not characterize reduced diagrams — Counterevidence: Aloop-typecurl addsZ butabridge-typecurl doesnot; reduced=>n0 remains. The recursiveordinaryedgebase is explicitlyallowed.
P5 — Positive-definite correction-term inequality reversed — Counterevidence: Later cubiquity uses the sharp equality c1^2=b2, not the wrong direction; this example does not refute that argument.

P5 — Positive-definite correction-term inequality reversed — Counterevidence: Theorem6.1choosessharpextensiongivingc1?-n=4d=0;Lemma6.3gluesbysharpequality;Lemma6.4usesd-invariantequality. None ofthese checkedsteps uses theincorrectdirection.
Limitations: Accepted author PDF reviewed; publisher VOR unavailable. Separate arXiv v2 source compared only in explicit portions; no whole-version equivalence.
Limitations: Proposition5.1 n=0 base and identification of a specified diagram from its lattice remain insufficiently verified; no concrete counterexample established and no extra Problem asserted.
Limitations: External Hajos, Donaldson, Floer sharpness, graph-lattice rigidity, flyping and branched-cover proofs not all independently reconstructed.
Limitations: All eight figures actually inspected; every Kirby blow-down and framing in Figure8 not independently replayed.
Limitations: Twelve-crossing census not rerun; algorithm complexity not benchmarked; author source not executed.
Limitations: Bounded metadata/correction/supplement search found no separate correction or executable supplement. Absence of code is not a mathematical defect.
Limitations: Initial scientific review only; no independent acceptance or authenticated backend equivalence.
The finding applies to the exact reviewed source version and inspected scope; uninspected publication versions are not adjudicated.
The report retains counterevidence and unresolved questions. Publication does not repeat scientific review.
Independent human scientific adjudication remains pending; author adoption has not been requested.
